# Test Fixtures

Each subdirectory is one self-contained test case named `<N>_<name>/`.

## Files in every fixture

| File | Purpose | Regeneratable? |
|---|---|---|
| `<name>_data.xlsx` | The source Excel file the engine extracts data from. Primary input used in all tests. | No — defines the test case |
| `<name>_data-cdr.xlsx` | Security CDR copy — macros, VBA, and external links stripped by OPSWAT MetaDefender, then reconstructed from safe content only. Used to test the security layer. | No — produced by external CDR tool |
| `<name>_pattern-from-draft.xlsx/.csv` | Legacy baseline pattern. For fixtures 01–14 this was authored as Python code in `scripts/generate_fixtures.py`; for 15–22 it was produced by `grepxcel draft` with an unrecorded backend. The `.xlsx` and `.csv` twins contain identical content. | Yes — see script |
| `<name>_pattern-from-claude.xlsx/.csv` | Pattern generated by the Claude API backend (`--backend claude`). Produced by `scripts/regenerate_drafts.py --backend claude`. | Yes — `regenerate_drafts.py` |
| `<name>_pattern-from-local.xlsx/.csv` | Pattern generated by the local LLM backend (`--backend local`, llama-cpp). Produced by `scripts/regenerate_drafts.py --backend local`. | Yes — `regenerate_drafts.py` |
| `<name>_pattern-from-github.xlsx/.csv` | Pattern generated by the GitHub Models backend (`--backend github`). | Yes — `regenerate_drafts.py` |
| `<name>_pattern-manual.xlsx` | **Hand-crafted** pattern by the project maintainer. Present only in fixtures 19–22. **Never overwrite or delete.** Protected by CLAUDE.md. | ❌ Read-only |
| `<name>_snapshot-from-<backend>.json` | Stored extraction result produced by running the engine with the corresponding `pattern-from-<backend>.*` file. Used by `test_snapshots.py` for regression testing. Generated by `scripts/generate_snapshots.py`. | Yes — `generate_snapshots.py` |
| `<name>_snapshot-manual.json` | Stored extraction result using the `pattern-manual.xlsx`. | Yes — `generate_snapshots.py` |

## Why `.xlsx` and `.csv` for patterns?

grepxcel accepts patterns in both `.xlsx` and `.csv` format. Every pattern variant
keeps an `.xlsx` and `.csv` twin — identical content, different format — so tests
can verify both parsers produce the same extraction result (see `test_csv_pattern_parity.py`).
The CSV twin is also the human-readable, diff-friendly representation.

## On-demand tooling

| Task | Script |
|---|---|
| Regenerate a draft pattern for a fixture | `python3 scripts/regenerate_drafts.py <fixture> --backend claude\|local\|github` |
| Refresh extraction snapshots after a pattern or engine change | `python3 scripts/generate_snapshots.py <fixture> [--source <backend\|manual>]` |
| Extract to xlsx/csv/json for human review | `grepxcel extract -p <pattern> <data> --format xlsx -o review/` |

These scripts are NOT run in CI — LLM calls and intentional snapshot refreshes are always manual.
